source.scope: Source-aligned argument for irrational_sqrt_two and its square criteria. Edges summarize selected proof steps and source references.

nodes.name: irrational_sqrt_two
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational (√2) := by
  simpa using Nat.prime_two.irrational_sqrt

nodes.name: Square the rational witness
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonneg {q : ℚ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) :
    Irrational (√q) ↔ ¬IsSquare q := by
  refine Iff.not (?_ : Exists _ ↔ Exists _)
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
    refine ⟨y, Rat.cast_injective (α := ℝ) ?_⟩
    rw [Rat.cast_mul, hy, mul_self_sqrt (Rat.cast_nonneg.2 hq)]
  · rintro ⟨q', rfl⟩
    exact ⟨|q'|, mod_cast (sqrt_mul_self_eq_abs q').symm⟩

nodes.name: Transfer squarehood to ℕ
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff {n : ℕ} : Irrational (√n) ↔ ¬IsSquare n := by
  rw [← Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff, ← irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonneg n.cast_nonneg,
    Rat.cast_natCast]

nodes.name: A prime is not a square
nodes.lean:
theorem Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) : Irrational (√p) :=
  irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.mpr hp.not_isSquare

nodes.name: Specialize at two
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational (√2) := by
  simpa using Nat.prime_two.irrational_sqrt

lean:irrational_sqrt_two.title: Irrationality of √2
lean:irrational_sqrt_two.summary: No rational number equals the nonnegative real square root of 2. The proof applies the irrationality theorem for prime square roots using the fact that 2 is prime.
lean:irrational_sqrt_two.why_here: This is the theorem established by the concluding fact.

lean:Irrational.title: Irrational real numbers
lean:Irrational.summary: A real number is irrational if there is no rational number whose image in the reals equals it.
lean:Irrational.why_here: Unfolding the definition lets the rational criterion be proved by comparing two kinds of witnesses.

lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.title: Rational square criterion
lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.summary: For a nonnegative rational number, its real square root is irrational exactly when the number has no rational square witness.
lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.compact_latex: \sqrt q\notin\mathbb Q\iff\nexists y\in\mathbb Q\; (y^2=q)\qquad(q\in\mathbb Q,\ q\ge0)
lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.why_here: The rational-witness argument establishes this equivalence.

lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.title: Squarehood under rational casting
lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.summary: A natural number has a rational square witness exactly when it has a natural square witness. This identifies the two squarehood tests for the same natural number.
lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.why_here: This equivalence replaces the rational squarehood condition with the natural one.

lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.title: Natural square criterion
lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.summary: The real square root of a natural number is irrational exactly when the number has no natural square witness.
lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.why_here: The transfer step establishes this equivalence, and the prime argument uses the direction from nonsquare to irrational.

lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.title: Prime square roots
lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.summary: Every prime natural number has an irrational real square root.
lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.why_here: The prime argument establishes this general result, which is then applied to 2.

lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.title: Irreducible elements are nonsquares
lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.summary: If an irreducible element factored as a square, irreducibility would force its repeated factor to be a unit. The square would then also be a unit, contradicting irreducibility.
lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.why_here: The graph identifies this nonsquare principle as support for the prime-root argument.

lean:Nat.prime_two.title: 2 is prime
lean:Nat.prime_two.summary: This theorem supplies primality for the specific natural number 2.
lean:Nat.prime_two.why_here: The primality step cites this theorem to supply the hypothesis for specialization.

step:rational-square.title: Convert square-root witnesses
step:rational-square.summary: Take a nonnegative rational q. If the real square root of q equals a rational y, squaring gives y² = q because the real square root squares to q and the rational embedding is injective. Conversely, from a rational square witness q = (q′)², the rational number |q′| equals the real square root of q. Negating the equivalence between witness existence statements gives the irrationality criterion.
step:rational-square.why_here: This proves the rational criterion by unfolding irrationality and converting witnesses in both directions.

fact:rational-square.title: Nonnegative rational criterion
fact:rational-square.summary: For any nonnegative rational q, its real square root is irrational exactly when q is a nonsquare in the rationals.
fact:rational-square.compact_latex: \sqrt q\notin\mathbb Q\iff\nexists y\in\mathbb Q\; (y^2=q)\qquad(q\in\mathbb Q,\ q\ge0)
fact:rational-square.why_here: This is the result of the witness conversion and the premise used to obtain the natural criterion.

step:natural-square.title: Transfer the criterion to naturals
step:natural-square.summary: View an arbitrary natural number n as a nonnegative rational and apply the rational criterion. Its casts through the rationals and directly into the reals give the same square-root input. The squarehood transfer lemma replaces rational squarehood with natural squarehood, yielding the criterion for n.
step:natural-square.why_here: This connects the rational witness argument to the natural-number condition used for primes.

fact:natural-square.title: Natural square criterion
fact:natural-square.summary: For every natural number n, the real square root of n is irrational exactly when no natural number squares to n.
fact:natural-square.why_here: This is the transferred equivalence used to turn the nonsquare property of a prime into irrationality.

step:prime-root.title: Apply the criterion to a prime
step:prime-root.summary: Assume p is a prime natural number. A factorization p = m² would give two copies of the same factor, so primality would force m = 1 and hence p = 1, which is impossible for a prime. The nonsquare-to-irrational direction of the natural criterion now gives irrationality of √p.
step:prime-root.why_here: This discharges the squarehood condition using primality and produces the general prime-root result.

fact:prime-root.title: Prime square roots are irrational
fact:prime-root.summary: For any natural number p with a proof of primality, its real square root is irrational.
fact:prime-root.why_here: This general result supplies the rule applied at 2.

step:two-prime.title: Use the primality of 2
step:two-prime.summary: The step takes the established theorem that 2 is prime and supplies that same fact as a premise for specialization. The supplied graph gives no separate primality derivation.
step:two-prime.why_here: This forwards the named primality theorem to the premise used in the final step.

fact:two-prime.title: Primality of 2
fact:two-prime.summary: The specific natural number 2 satisfies the primality hypothesis of the prime-root theorem.
fact:two-prime.why_here: This supplies the concrete primality premise for the specialization.

step:specialize.title: Specialize the prime-root theorem at 2
step:specialize.summary: The general prime-root theorem takes a natural number together with its primality proof. Substituting 2 and using the supplied proof of its primality yields that the real square root of 2 is irrational.
step:specialize.why_here: This combines the general theorem with the primality of 2 to produce the concluding fact.

fact:specialize.title: Irrationality of √2
fact:specialize.summary: The real square root of 2 has no rational representative.
fact:specialize.why_here: This is the output of specialization and states exactly the root theorem.

concepts.title: Irrationality as absence of a rational representative
concepts.summary: A real number is irrational when no rational number maps to it under the embedding of the rationals into the reals. An equivalence about the existence of rational representatives can be negated to obtain an irrationality criterion.

concepts.title: Square witnesses and absolute value
concepts.summary: For a nonnegative rational q, a rational representative y of √q gives a rational square witness by squaring. In the reverse direction, any rational y satisfying y² = q gives |y| as a rational representative of √q, since the real square root is nonnegative.

concepts.title: Squarehood across natural and rational numbers
concepts.summary: A natural number is a square in the rationals exactly when it is a square in the naturals. Consequently the square-root criterion for a rational input can be expressed using natural square witnesses when the input comes from the naturals.

concepts.title: Prime numbers are nonsquares
concepts.summary: A square factorization of a prime would repeat a factor, and primality forces that factor to be 1. This would make the prime itself 1, so the natural square criterion implies that every prime has an irrational square root.
